messages.subject: Re: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
messages.subject_clean: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
messages.body_plain:
The Processing.R project is still hoping to run some tests on R packages that are fully compatible with renjin.

1. Is there a way to find a listing from packages.renjin.org <http://packages.renjin.org/> of anything that "passed all tests" -- for example, by querying the build system?
2. If not, do renjin devs know of a short list of any R packages that might be expected to just work out-of-the-box when imported in renjin? Even 2-3 suggestions would be a helpful place to start.

Many thanks,
Jeremy

Just as the "Processing.py" Python Mode uses Jython to enable Processing-in-Python, the "Processing.R" R Language Mode uses Renjin to enable coding Processing-in-R. Part of the early work is in mapping out calls to the Processing(Java) API -- e.g. `processing$line(x,y,x2,y2)` -- and later in using pre-processing to make the API automagically available as a top-level namespace.

messages.subject: Re: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
messages.subject_clean: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeremy,

why don't you try http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/plyr which is a popular package and which depends on Rcpp. It should work close to 100%.

There are also a couple of packages for which we provide drop-in replacements such as digest, rjson, and xml2. These may not implement the full functionality of the original R packages (e.g. xml2 has only a small subset of functions), but do work. They tend to be mostly infrastructure packages whose GNU R versions interface with system libraries.

Given that Processing.org is primarily used to create visuals, you should probably look at packages which provide interesting statistical models. So the built-in stats package should be on your list (e.g. to sample from different types of random variables) as well.

Other (near) 100% compatibility packages based on a totally random look through our package browser:
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/changepoint
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/foreach
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/GeneF
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/uniftest
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/orthopolynom
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/magrittr
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/rateratio.test
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/regexr
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/rlm
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/optR
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/outliers
Hope this helps!
​
Maarten

I am integrating my R scripts with Renjin, problem is that I am sourcing 25 files which are interconnected. on final execution If I am getting any error, I am unable to figure out form which file/function or line of code it is coming. is there any way that I can run this script on debug mode on renjin.

I have tried executing these scripts on R studio there they are running fine without any error.

Any pointer or support is welcome to tackle this situation.

Thanks in advance.

messages.subject: Re: Debug mode on Renjin?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Anurag,

Unfortunately I don't have have an easy solution for you. Ruslan did some heroic <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/pull/64> work to add sourceRefs to the AST but I've had to remove most of it because I don't think we got the srcRef representation right and it led to errors elsewhere.

Anyway, the only two solutions currently are
1) Run in debug mode with a Java IDE
2) Old fashioned println debugging: Add cat("about to eval source file X.R\n") throughout your script to see how far you get.

If you use a Java IDE, set a breakpoint for EvalException and then look for calls to the "evaluateCall" java method. You can then follow the R stack trace upward.

Hope this helps!

Alex

Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: ARIMA with Renjin
messages.body_plain:
It looks like the ARIMA function in the stats packages relies on the BFGS optimization routine which isn't currently implemented in Renjin.

I believe we just need to import the C code for the BFGS routine as the GCC-Bridge compiler should now be able to handle it, but this hasn't been done yet.

This is actually on my list for August, so check back then!

Best,
Alex
